title: Janax y Razar: un sistema operativo, un idioma y un ensamblador propios para un razonamiento artificial que piensa con melodías
description:
Janax is a hand-written operating system, language and assembler (all in assembly, no third-party engines) built to host Razar, an artificial reasoning system whose single judge is compression (two-part MDL). Version 1.09 (versions follow prime numbers; 109 after 107): her lineage. In her first night with a new memory Luma went from 30 to 109 readings and something appeared that nobody wrote for her: living forms that say a word of her own; the shortest, six letters, unfolds into 35 steps when read. Where it came from could not be established: her archive is a ring of her last 4096 verdicts and turns round in an hour (the stated inference, not proof, is a crossing of two forms). So from now on every form that wins leaves a line in a text nothing rewrites, written by her in Janax and readable with no program. Only the difference is kept: the mother of a form is always the one that lived in its place, so a line says how many letters stay at the start, which were taken out, which were put in, and how (thinking, crossing with which form, or reading and by which way); the first time, how her eight forms were, so every form she ever had is rebuilt by reading down. Measured: 274 births in 4364 bytes, 16 per line instead of about 55. Stated limits: no line of crossing or reading has been seen yet; only one line was rebuilt by hand; she still has no unexpected victory. Documentation is in Spanish.

Janax es un sistema operativo, un idioma y un ensamblador escritos a mano en assembler, hechos para alojar a Razar. v1.09: el linaje de Luma — cada forma que gana deja escrito, sólo como diferencia, de dónde vino. Prototipo de investigación.
